svg.aria-label: Most common owner complaints about smart glasses, ranked qualitatively

g.text: What smart-glasses owners complain about most (recent 1–3★ reviews and owner threads)
Occasional
Common
Very common
Battery: dead by mid-afternoon
Gen 1 Ray-Bans ran ~4 h; Gen 2 doubled it. Live AI and video eat a charge in 30–60 min on any brand. The case is not optional.
AI that misunderstands, or answers "I can't help with that"
Meta AI is conservative; Rokid's ChatGPT/Gemini switch is praised. Every brand's AI is worse in noise and with accents.
Features promised, not yet delivered (phased rollouts, regions)
Meta unlocks features server-side by region and account; Gen 2 owners waited months for 5-min clips and 1080p60. Kickstarter brands ship late.
Prescription: range limits and the real cost
Display is −4 to +4 only; Rx lenses add $45–$210 (retrofit) to $200–$400 (optician). Progressives are hit-or-miss on all of them.
Sound leaks; people nearby hear your call
Open-ear speakers by design. Keep volume under 60% in quiet rooms; the Vanguard is the loudest — and leakiest.
Weight, nose pressure, heat on the temples
69 g Display and 87 g Xreal draw the most; 49 g Rokid and Gen 2 Wayfarers the least. Low-bridge-fit frames matter for many Asian and flat-bridge faces.
Being asked to remove them — social and venue friction
Rising fast in 2026 reviews: gyms, courts, cinemas, a friend's living room. Camera-free models avoid it.
Photo/video quality in low light; Wi-Fi transfer slow
"Phone-adjacent, not camera-quality." Fine in daylight, grainy at dinner. Transfers to the phone app take minutes for 3K clips.
Qualitative ranking of themes across recent Amazon 1–3★ reviews, Meta community forums and Reddit owner threads for the glasses in this guide — a tally, not a survey.
